'''''Gnaphalium''''' is a [[genus]] of [[flowering plant]]s in the family [[Asteraceae]],<ref name=o/><ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/358871#page/292/mode/1up Linnaeus, Carl von. 1753.  Species Plantarum 2: 850-857] in Latin</ref> commonly called '''cudweeds''' or (formerly) '''chafeweeds'''. They are widespread and common in [[temperate]] regions, although some are found on tropical mountains or in the subtropical regions of the world.

== Secondary metabolites ==
''Gnaphalium'' species are known to contain [[flavonoids]] and [[diterpenes]]. Recently, two unique caffeoyl-D-glucaric acid derivatives, leontopodic acid and leontopodic acid B formerly only known from ''[[Leontopodium alpinum]]'' (L.) Cass. were detected in various species of ''Gnaphalium'' together with similar formerly unknown compounds.<ref>{{cite journal |date=July 2012 |author1=Cicek, S |author2=Untersulzner, C |author3=Schwaiger, S |author4=Zidorn, C | title = Caffeoyl-D-glucaric acid derivatives in the genus Gnaphalium (Asteraceae: Gnaphalieae) | volume = 6 | issue = 3 | pages = 311–315 | issn = 1307-6167 | journal = Records of Natural Products (Gebze-Kocaeli, Türkiye) | url = http://www.acgpubs.org/RNP/2012/Volume%206/Issue%201/44-RNP-1102-492.pdf | format = Free full text }}</ref>
